The Supreme Court will let Donald Trump continue building his White House ballroom and “military complex” while a legal challenge against the East Wing’s demolition and sprawling construction project continues.

Friday’s one-page decision from Chief Justice John Roberts gives the president permission to keep building what his administration is increasingly describing as a highly fortified military installation that is vital to the safety and security of the president.

A months-long legal battle has stalled construction, but the president urged the Supreme Court last week to intervene and let him build what he has called a “desperately needed National Security structure” — including a massive underground bunker and rooftop military complex with a bulletproof, hermetically sealed ballroom built with nuclear-blast-resistant materials sandwiched in between.

On August 7, a federal appeals court in Washington, D.C. ordered the government to stop construction on the project by Friday unless Congress — or the Supreme Court — stepped in.

With Friday’s order, the administration can continue construction while the Supreme Court considers its next steps. The justices and federal court judges will likely hear more arguments over the plans and whether Trump subverted the role of Congress with his unilateral decision to demolish the East Wing.

open image in gallery The Supreme Court will temporarily allow Donald Trump’s administration to continue construction on a $400 million ballroom and military site after demolishing the East Wing of the White House ( Reuters )

Trump’s plans initially envisioned an ornate White House ballroom stuffed with gold finishes and marble floors, but court filings over the last several months have detailed what officials called “top secret” designs that revealed the primary purpose of the 90,000-square-foot ballroom project.

The president told reporters at the White House on Monday that military officials approached him with plans for the military complex after he announced his intentions to build a ballroom last year.

He said he was told there is an “opportunity to build deep into the ground and build a military facility to go with the White House — and to go with all of Washington, D.C., which would be so valuable.”

open image in gallery Trump and administration officials are increasingly characterizing the ballroom as a military complex vital to national security, with plans for a massive underground bunker, nuclear-blast-resistant construction materials and a ‘drone port’ on the roof ( AP )

The ballroom is “a knitted, unified, cohesive part of the East Wing Project, which is vital for National Security, and is being constructed to ensure that the President can perform his constitutional duties in a safe and heavily secured facility,” government lawyers wrote in court documents this summer.

The project will include“heavy steel, drone-proof roof, missile-resistant and drone-proof columns, bullet, ballistic, and blast-proof glass, Military-grade venting for air conditioning and heating” as well as “bomb shelters, a state of the art hospital and medical facilities, Top Secret military installations, structures, and equipment, protective partitioning, and other features,” according to the Department of Justice.

If the Supreme Court didn’t halt construction, the project “will in all likelihood become irreversible,” preservationists who sued the administration wrote to the justices this week.

open image in gallery Trump had urged the Supreme Court to step in to save his ‘desperately needed’ ballroom after federal courts repeatedly halted the project, arguing that he wrongfully pursued the plans without congressional authorization ( AFP/Getty )

Because the construction materials are meant to withstand even nuclear blasts, there would be no way to take any of it down even if the courts intervened later, the group argued.

The National Trust for Historic Preservation said the administration’s “striking admission” that the project is “on the brink of a fait accompli” is precisely why the Supreme Court must stop construction now.

“The question is simply who decides whether a ballroom can be built on federal property. Our constitutional system and federal law commits that choice to Congress,” the group wrote.

There is nothing that prevents the president from asking Congress for one — “today, tomorrow, or any time in the future,” they added.

But Trump’s attempt to “foil judicial review and arrogate Congress’s exclusive powers should not be rewarded” with a court order that allows him to continue construction that he lacked “any authority to commence in the first place,” the group argued.

Federal courts have now repeatedly blocked parts of the project from moving forward without approval from Congress, but Democratic and Republican leaders don’t seem interested in getting involved.

“We don’t believe we have to go to Congress. We believe Congress has already given us the authority to do what we’re doing,” Attorney General Todd Blanche said during an appearance on Fox News Sunday. “Many presidents have done a tremendous amount of work to the White House, as they should, and Congress has authorized them to do so.”

Costs for the project have exploded from an initial $200 million estimate to $400 million — with some believing it could cost upwards of $600 million.

While Trump has said private donations will pay for the ballroom itself, the administration transferred more than $300 million from the Secret Service budget to cover security upgrades to the White House this summer.

News.title: Root delivers perfect riposte to captaincy doubters as England hammer Pakistan
News.content:
There was no attempt to be a Ben Stokes tribute act by Joe Root, just a measured captaincy performance very much in his own undemonstrative style.

Root, ever the team man, pushed his bowlers forward to lead England off at the end, recognising the match-winners in a walkover against Pakistan, who were bowled out for 135 in under two sessions.

Victory by an innings and 103 runs inside three days marked a perfect return to the job and put the smile back on England faces for the first time in a long while. The chants of “F--- the ECB” from Trent Bridge, after the New Zealand regime-toppling loss, were replaced by the Yorkshire faithful’s “Roooot”.

There was plenty of scepticism around rebooting the Root captaincy, but he was the only realistic choice. Harry Brook’s batting here was more sensible and at a tempo in the captain’s mould. “He is still learning the art of Test cricket,” Root said. Thrusting Brook into the job would have put more pressure on him, he may well have felt he needed to make risky statements with the bat. Now he can mature under Root and Stephen Fleming.

Tactically, Root was astute and showed enough to suggest he is going to be different this time. The old Root would not have whipped Jofra Archer off after two overs of the Test, but it was a prod that worked as he bowled quicker and more accurately to strike twice with the second-innings new ball, using his new-found skills with a scrambled seam to good effect.

It also showed his bowlers he wanted a fuller length and, from that first hour, they controlled the match and did not let their grip slip.

Root promised to keep the good aspects of Bazball and apply common sense. He continued Stokes’s leg-slip tactic and it paid off with the wicket of opener Azan Awais, and urged Ollie Robinson to bowl with the keeper standing up. England batted at 4.5 an over – a touch quicker than the Bazball years – but it was never reckless, just a calm tempo, with no ramps or scoops.

News.title: Russell takes Dutch GP sprint pole as Antonelli struggles to fifth
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for sprint qualifying for the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix from Zandvoort. This is the last time the race will be on the F1 calendar for the foreseeable future, having been reintroduced in 2021 after a 35-year absence. It will be a shame to see it leave again, but never rule out it coming back, especially with Max Verstappen signing a lengthy contract extension with Red Bull.

What of the competitive action this weekend? As it is a sprint weekend, there is not a lot of preparation time, with just one practice session before sprint qualifying. In that it was a fairly close fight at the top, and it was Kimi Antonelli, the championship leader, who was fastest of all. Behind him was the McLaren of Lando Norris who was 0.121sec adrift then George Russell, who will be looking to kickstart his title campaign here, a further 0.004sec behind him.

Then came the two Ferraris of Lewis Hamilton (0.190sec) and Charles Leclerc (0.289sec) before a fairly significant gap of 0.659sec to Oscar Piastri in sixth. Verstappen was down in 11th, nearly 1.4sec off Antonelli’s ultimate pace but 0.5sec or so ahead of new (and old) team-mate for the weekend, Liam Lawson.

It was a tricky session for the drivers, though, as it began damp on a showery and blustery day by the Dutch seaside. Several drivers ran wide and off the track, though they all avoided anything more serious than gravel rash. The rest of the day looks to be drier but there are still a few showers around and the wind is all over the place, as it often is here.

Sprint qualifying starts at 3.30pm BST and we will be here for all of the updates for the nearly hour-long session.

News.title: Officials selling yellow fever certificates to unvaccinated travellers
News.content:
Officials in Malawi are selling yellow fever certificates to unvaccinated travellers for around $20 and sending them on their way, a Telegraph investigation has found.



The passport-sized, yellow document, officially called the International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP), is supposed to provide proof of vaccination against yellow fever, a mosquito-borne virus that kills tens of thousands of people every year.

The jab provides lifelong protection, beginning 10 days after vaccination. Most countries in Africa and Latin America require them for entry, either for all travellers or for those arriving from risk areas.



Yet travellers leaving Malawi through two major airports can get hold of the certificates without ever being vaccinated, according to interviews with multiple travellers and an undercover investigation.



Several passengers who travelled recently from Malawi to destinations including Uganda, Kenya, Ethiopia and China said they had obtained yellow fever vaccination certificates at airports or public hospitals without receiving the vaccine.



One traveller, who recently flew to Uganda for work from Kamuzu International Airport, which serves the capital, Lilongwe, said he was initially told it was too late to get vaccinated because his departure was less than 10 days away.



“When I asked the health officials if I could get vaccinated at the airport, I was told it was too late because I needed to be vaccinated ten days before my trip,” he told The Telegraph.



“But then they offered to arrange the certificate for me for roughly $21,” said the traveller, who asked not to be named. “I had to pay because I could not postpone the trip.”

News.title: Congo gambles on ‘old’ vaccine as new Ebola virus spirals
News.content:
Nearly half of all those infected have gone on to die.

Dr Sania Nishtar, chief executive of the Gavi global vaccine partnership, earlier this week said to beat the outbreak “we must deploy every tool at our disposal”.

She went on: “To avoid this becoming the worst recorded Ebola outbreak in history, it is critical that all effective countermeasure options are brought to bear.

“We have a tool that could help save lives while we wait for [Bundibugyo]-specific vaccines to become available.”

Previous clinical trials have shown that Ervebo is safe, but its effect on other strains is unknown.

The World Health Organisation said in a statement that while it was not known if Ervebo may protect against the Bundibugyo virus, “early laboratory and animal data suggest it may provide some protection”.

Medics told the Telegraph of anecdotal claims that health workers who had been given Ervebo to protect them during an outbreak of the Zaire strain in 2018 to 2020 had not fallen ill during the current Bundibugyo outbreak.

Health workers are at extreme risk of catching the disease because they come into contact with highly-contagious blood, vomit and diarrhoea from dying patients. When they fall sick themselves, they frequently go on to infect their own families.

Giving health workers vaccine jabs to protect them as they tend the sick is a cornerstone of Ebola responses.

The WHO said the vaccine allocation includes 20,000 doses for a Phase 3 clinical trial to understand the impact of the vaccine on the Bundibugyo virus. The remaining 50,000 doses will be used for front-line and health workers as recommended by WHO experts.

Dr Nishtar said: “Having already been licensed for the Zaire strain, we know that Ervebo is proven to be safe.

“And while the signs are that it may not stop transmission – which is essential for ending the outbreak - it could well save precious lives and reduce suffering.”

Health officials warn that the Bundibugyo outbreak centred on DRC’s Ituri province is easily outpacing relief efforts.

The virus is thought to have been spreading for months before an outbreak was finally declared in mid-May and medics have been unable to make up the head start.

An analysis by the Africa Centres for Disease Control meanwhile warned the current outbreak dwarfed all others on record

The current outbreak had almost ten times more cases than any other previous outbreak at a similar stage.

News.title: Soaring welfare bill pushes national debt to almost £3tn
News.content:
Britain’s soaring welfare bill forced John Healey to borrow more to balance the books last month.

The gap between tax receipts and spending unexpectedly resulted in a £1.8bn deficit in July, taking the national debt to within a whisker of £3tn.

Economists had predicted the Government would borrow nothing and blamed the deficit on the rising welfare bill.

Figures published by the Office for National Statistics (ONS) this morning show total debt rose to £2.985tn in July.

Benefit payments also climbed by 7.2pc, or £2bn, to £30bn last month.

The Chancellor now faces another tax-raising Budget in October, even as strong receipts from self-employed workers provide some respite.

The ONS also said Mr Healey spent £7.7bn on debt interest in July alone, almost 10pc higher than a year ago.

Ashley Webb, at Capital Economics said: “The weak performance was mainly due higher social payments.”

Monthly borrowing was slightly higher than the Office for Budget Responsibility and markets expected, meaning the Government has borrowed £56.7bn this financial year to plug the gap between tax receipts and public spending.

Julian Jessop, an independent economist and IEA economics fellow, said: “The latest official data highlight the fragility of the public finances as John Healey prepares his first Budget. Government borrowing was £2.3bn above forecast in July, and £0.7bn higher than in the same month a year ago.”

July is traditionally a strong month for receipts from the self-employed, with self-assessed income tax receipts last month coming to £17.1bn, about £1.7bn more than a year earlier.

However, higher inflation triggered by the Iran war means Mr Healey will be forced to use the Budget to find billions of pounds to repair the public finances.

Mr Healey said: “Fiscal discipline is the bedrock of our UK economic stability and national security which is why we are committed to meeting our fiscal rules, with a buffer against global uncertainties.”

The Resolution Foundation warned that the Chancellor’s headroom against his fiscal rules - self-imposed guardrails to guide public spending - has shrunk from around £24bn in the Spring Statement to less than £8bn today.

The think tank called on the Chancellor to use his first Budget on Oct 28 to put the nation’s finances on a more sustainable path.

Elliott Christensen, senior economist at the Resolution Foundation, said: “The Chancellor’s margin against his fiscal rules is now razor thin.”

News.title: Brook falls agonisingly short of Headingley hundred again as England continue to dominate
News.content:
“Yeah, of course I did,” said Cox, when asked if he was frustrated to miss out on three figures. Cox was caught behind off spinner Ali Usman, but believed he had hit his pad with his bat, not the ball.

“Once I got to fifty, I moved to sixty quickly, and thought ‘there’s a chance here’. Just keep being disciplined, ball by ball. I had it at the back of my mind, thinking you have worked so hard, do not give this opportunity up. That is exactly what I do in county cricket. I get to fifty, see how many runs I need to score, and work down from there.”

Asked if his team-mates were feeling the same emotion, he said: “Oh yeah there is. Every team, every player wants to score Test hundreds. Four of us got fifties, so we were hoping one would kick on, and instead of making it just a hundred, make it 150 or 170.

“I am thrilled. I would have taken it at the start of the Test match. I let myself down a tiny bit, but at the end of the day, you take 70.”

Cox resumed on day two on 23, then was dropped by the bowler Khurram Shahzad on 57. In the course of his innings, he was compared to AB de Villiers by the former England captain Michael Vaughan.

Cox is likely to get a good run across formats. England had hoped to call on Sam Curran for the third Test of this series, but his summer is over due to a groin injury. Curran will undergo surgery on Friday.

It is likely England will be without Curran, Bethell and Tom Banton for September’s white-ball series against Sri Lanka, which should mean greater opportunity for the likes of Cox and Sussex’s James Coles, and could even see a recall for Zak Crawley, who made an assured 81 for Kent against Middlesex on Thursday. Will Jacks is currently sidelined with appendicitis, but is expected to have recovered in time for the series.

News.title: Robinson demolishes Pakistan to cement importance to new regime
News.content:
He also has that edge, the grunt of an angry fast bowler, and his competitiveness was just what Root needed considering his other quicks were still in Hundred mode. Archer bowled too short, Gus Atkinson grew into the innings but was wicketless and it took a while for Tongue to click, although once he did he was unplayable against the right-handers with his pace and angle.

Robinson’s lack of pace gives them the keeper-standing-up option. It worked a treat when he bowled Pakistan’s top-scorer, Abdullah Shafique for 61, his footwork messed up by Jamie Smith breathing down his neck.

Pakistan would have batted first had they won the toss and it is a good pitch that will improve as the Test goes on, although with rain around all week the overheads will have a say on the game. Pakistan have far more recent red-ball exposure than England’s batsmen but they were ill-equipped to deal with Robinson and Tongue.

Most supporters were still walking into the ground when the former struck first ball, Azan Awais lbw to a nip-backer. Shan Masood’s stilted footwork was ripe for exposing and Robinson’s first ball over the wicket to the left-hander was full and straight to beat the loose drive.

Imam-ul-Haq had done the hard work, seeing off Robinson only to flash a drive to second slip off a wide ball from Tongue to end Pakistan’s only stand of substance of the innings: 93 for the third wicket.

Robinson cracked the innings open further with Saud Shakeel leg before, who was too slow to call for the review that would have saved him. Hawk-Eye showed the ball would have gone over the top.

Robinson then bowled Shafique in his next over and Pakistan were toppling. Tongue cranked up the pace, bowled full and the perpendicular angle into the right-handers did the rest.

Sports.title: Man United set for transfer windfall thanks to sell-on clause as player in 'advanced talks'
Sports.content:
Man United set for transfer windfall thanks to sell-on clause as player in 'advanced talks'

Manchester United's transfer funds could receive a boost before the end of the summer window as they benefit from a deal agreed in 2024

View 2 Images Michael Carrick's Man United transfer kitty could receive a boost (Image: Marc Atkins, Getty Images)

Manchester United are set to see their transfer funds boosted when Willy Kambwala finalises his departure from Villarreal. Kambwala, 21, is on course to join Italian side Como and United will cash in thanks to having the foresight to include a sell-on clause.

‌



Como are looking likely to pip Spanish club Osasuna to his signing and the Red Devils will pocket. United sources described the sell-on clause for Kambwala as "sizeable" when he departed the club two years ago after making his debut aged 19.

‌



However, Villarreal are only expected to take in a modest fee, limiting the amount that United will receive. Kambwala departed Old Trafford in 2024 when the Yellow Submarine came in for the player.

‌



Villarreal tabled an offer of €5.5million (£4.7m) plus €6m (£5.14m) in add-ons to acquire Kambwala from United. The agreement incorporated a buy-back option and matching rights for three years, alongside the sizeable sell-on clause.

United occasionally included clauses in player sales prior to Sir Jim Ratcliffe's investment in the club, but it has since become standard practice following Ineos taking charge of football operations It is now a crucial part of negotiations when players head out of the club.

United included a "high percentage" sell-on clause and buyback option in the sale of Tyler Fredricson to Lausanne-Sport, with comparable clauses also written into the sale of Radek Vitek to Middlesbrough.

‌



United inserted a buy-back clause into the deal with Boro, along with matching rights and a sell-on clause of up to 35 per cent to profit from any potential future sale. Ethan Williams was transferred to Peterborough last week, with United inserting a 50 per cent sell-on clause into the agreement, alongside a buyback option and matching rights clauses.

Ethan Ennis completed a permanent switch to Stockport County earlier this week. United included a 50 per cent sell-on clause in that deal, as well as buyback and matching rights clauses.

View 2 Images Willy Kambwala left Manchester United in 2024 (Image: Getty)

‌

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Neville asked a leading question about Vinicius to Wright at the start of Sky Sports pre-match coverage of their Premier League opener against Coventry City. After Neville said: "Who are they bringing in?" Wright replied: "This is what I am saying.

"They were talking about...I don't know if Alvarez is coming. Obviously, then went for Vini, I know that was happening, people laughed at me. You two laughed."

‌



After Carragher snapped back: "That was never happening" Wright then replied: "At some stage, Ill show you, I'll show you the proof."

View 3 Images Vini Jr remained at Real Madrid amid interest from Arsenal (Image: Antonio Villalba/Real Madrid via Getty Images)

Wright did not divulge what exactly his proof was in regards to Vinicius, at one stage of the saga, heading to Arsenal this summer. He signed a new six-year deal to remain at the Bernabeu instead of moving to north London.

‌



Vinicius Jr was the second big name attacker to snub Arsenal, after Morgan Rogers opted to move to Chelsea for £117m. The Gunners have now switched their focus to Alvarez, which is proving to be another drawn out transfer saga.

Atletico did not include him in their La Liga opener against Malaga, after Diego Simeone stated the World Cup winner was not in the right frame of mind to compete.

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta's Arsenal pursued a move for Vinicius Jr (Image: 2026 The Arsenal Football Club Plc)

‌



After Wright told Carragher and Neville about his transfer "proof" he then added: "That's where we're going. I don't think we need to change the way we are playing, I just think we need to bring in that calibre of player to force it home."

One new signing who is already exciting Arsenal fans is Greek winger Christos Tzolis. His arrival from Club Brugge took place somewhat under the radar, as Arsenal were in the middle of the Vinicius and Rogers transfer sagas.

Sports.title: Liverpool learn Yankuba Minteh price tag after Brighton reject second transfer bid
Sports.content:
Liverpool learn Yankuba Minteh price tag after Brighton reject second transfer bid

Liverpool have seen their second bid for Yankuba Minteh rejected by Brighton, who have made their valuation known as the Reds scour the market for more attacking quality

View 2 Images Liverpool are chasing Brighton's Yankuba Minteh

Brighton have rejected a second bid from Liverpool for Yankuba Minteh, with the Seagulls insisting they want £70million for the winger.

‌



The Reds are in the market for attacking reinforcements and have identified the Brighton star as a target. They saw an opening offer of £50m turned down and, despite adding £10m onto that fee, those at the Amex have again rejected it.

‌



Minteh is currently sidelined after undergoing surgery on a right leg injury which means he will miss between two and three months of action. Last term the Brighton winger scored three goals, which did include a goal drought that ran for six months, and provided four assists in 36 games.

‌



Brighton signed Minteh from Newcastle back in 2024 and want to maximise their profits on a player they paid £30m for. The Seagulls are now looking to more than double their money. A £70m fee would make the Gambian the club's second largest sale, behind only Moises Caicedo.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The Athletic reports that it is unclear whether those from Liverpool will return with a third bid, despite an obvious desire to bolster their frontline. Brighton are also having to deal with interest in Carlos Baleba with the midfielder the subject of a £65m bid from Manchester United.

‌



Asked about Minteh and Baleba on Friday, Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said: "We know in general all the players there are rumours about, they are important players for us because they're a big part of the journey the last two years.

"In football, you have to understand, it's normal if you're successful as a team, if the team is doing well, they've had some good achievements, then an individual can shine. Then of course there will be a big ask for our players, that's part of our identity and part of my job here.

"It was clear for everyone this might happen during a busy transfer window. We can go through every individual player, we all know how important these kinds of players are for me, but we also know that good achievements, big achievements, especially in the Premier League, you create offers, you create a lot of attention."

‌



View 2 Images Bradley Barcola has been on Liverpool's radar all summer (Image: Giuseppe Maffia/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

The Reds have seen the legendary Mohamed Salah depart, although his role was reduced as last season went on. In an effort to fill his void they have signed 23-year-old forward Victor Munoz from Osasuna but their main summer target has been PSG's Bradley Barcola.

The major issue has been the Parisian's price tag with the European champions wanting well in excess of £100m before they consider selling up. A potentially cheaper alternative for Liverpool is also at PSG in teenager Ibrahim Mbaye with the Senegalese teenager valued at £59m.

‌



Andoni Iraola has maintained that Liverpool will land some new faces, but accepts that certain moves take time and may drag on until the end of the transfer window.

"We will definitely sign some players," the Spaniard told Sky Sports. "Some deals you have to wait until the end. But the end is the important picture, the one we will have on September 1, because it is true that we are still quite thin."

Sports.title: Chelsea secure agreement to host Champions League games for Shakhtar Donetsk
Sports.content:
Chelsea secure agreement to host Champions League games for Shakhtar Donetsk

Shakhtar Donetsk will play their home Champions League games at Stamford Bridge after striking a deal with Chelsea, who failed to qualify for Europe

View 2 Images Stamford Bridge will host Champions League football this season

Chelsea will host Champions League football this season after they agreed to let Shakhtar Donetsk play their home games at Stamford Bridge.

‌



The Ukrainian side have not played a match at their home stadium, the Donbas Arena, for more than 12 years due to the Russian invasion into Ukraine.

‌



As a result they've played across Europe with Shakhtar having to call the likes of Hamburg and Warsaw their temporary homes. Now they'll call London their home for a year and have settled on using Chelsea's ground having also considered playing at Brentford’s Gtech Stadium.

‌



Chelsea endured a poor year last season, going through two permanent managers, which meant they finished down in tenth and thus failed to qualify for any kind of European football.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

That has left Stamford Bridge free on Champions League nights and the Blues have decided to allow Shakhtar to play their home games in west London with the group stage draw still to be made.

‌



A Chelsea statement read: "FC Shakhtar have played in countries across Europe and we look forward to welcoming them to London for their Champions League campaign this year. We will be working with the Shakhtar team closely over the coming weeks to ensure that matchdays run safely and smoothly for their team and supporters."

Shakhtar have only played once at Stamford Bridge, that coming in November 2012 when they were undone by a last minute Victor Moses header in a five-goal thriller.

View 2 Images Shakhtar Donetsk's only outing at Stamford Bridge came back in 2012

‌



Shakhtar themselves have thanked the Premier League side for the opportunity. They said: "Playing our Champions League home matches at Stamford Bridge is a special opportunity for Shakhtar. We are grateful to Chelsea Football Club for the opportunity to host our games at this special venue. Stamford Bridge is one of the most famous stadiums in world football, with an incredible history and atmosphere. We are convinced that Shakhtar’s matches in London will provide unforgettable emotions for Ukrainian and English fans."

The Ukrainian side's best effort in the Champions League came back in 2011, when they made the quarter-finals. They topped a group that included Arsenal, beating the north Londoners at home, before Pep Guardiola's Barcelona ended their journey.

Sports.title: Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler responds to Man Utd's bid for Carlos Baleba
Sports.content:
Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler responds to Man Utd's bid for Carlos Baleba

Manchester United have submitted an offer of £60million plus £5m in add-ons for Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba, who will sit out of their Premier League opener this weekend

View 3 Images Fabian Hurzeler spoke about transfer rumours involving his players (Image: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)

Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler refused to be drawn on Manchester United's interest in midfielder Carlos Baleba on the eve of their Premier League campaign.

‌



United have submitted an offer of £60million plus £5m in add-ons for the 22-year-old, who Michael Carrick wants to further bolster his midfield alongside new arrivals Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos.

‌



Baleba is keen on a move to Old Trafford and has reportedly already agreed personal terms. United first enquired about the Cameroon international last summer and are now confident they can wrap up a deal for considerably less than the £100m they were quoted 12 months ago.

‌



Hurzeler faced reporters on Friday ahead of Brighton's Premier League opener against Aston Villa on Sunday and didn't give much away, bar confirming Baleba would miss the game due to an ankle injury picked up in pre-season.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"He's a Brighton player. Like I said, I'll never comment on any rumours that are currently in the media, it's also something I definitely can't control," the German said.

"A lot of things are written, I know about situations but again, in two days I have a very important game together with my team and with my staff. We want to have a good start in the Premier League season, that's the only focus we have at the moment."

His words echoed those of Brighton chief executive Paul Barber the day before. "It’s not something that I can talk about right now," Barber told talkSPORT on Thursday.

‌



View 3 Images Manchester United are confident of signing Carlos Baleba (Image: Getty Images)

"This time of year we’re always going to be subject to bids for our players, we’re always going to be interested in ones that are sensible and are going to make sense for us financially, economically. But we also have to balance that with making sure our squad is as strong as it can be to compete in competitions like the one we’re in.

"So nothing really to say on Carlos at the moment other than that he’s a hugely talented young midfielder who’s done really well for us and has attracted interest from some of the biggest clubs in the world now for a couple of years."

‌



Brighton are also fielding interest from Liverpool in winger Yankuba Minteh. The Seagulls have rejected a £50m bid from Andoni Iraola's side and know the transfer game better than most, having lost many key players to Premier League rivals in recent years.

View 3 Images Yankuba Minteh is wanted by Liverpool (Image: Crystal Pix/MB Media/Getty Images)

"We know in general all the players there are rumours about, they are important players for us because they're a big part of the journey the last two years," Hurzeler said.

‌



"In football, you have to understand, it's normal if you're successful as a team, if the team is doing well, they've had some good achievements, then an individual can shine. Then of course there will be a big ask for our players, that's part of our identity and part of my job here.

"It was clear for everyone this might happen during a busy transfer window. We can go through every individual player, we all know how important these kinds of players are for me, but we also know that good achievements, big achievements, especially in the Premier League, you create offers, you create a lot of attention."

Sports.title: Ezri Konsa recalls earning approval of Arsenal star after one-on-one session
Sports.content:
Ezri Konsa recalls earning approval of Arsenal star after one-on-one session

Ezri Konsa's defensive quality has previously been hailed by Bukayo Saka, with Arsenal now signing the England international from Aston Villa for over £50million

View 2 Images Ezri Konsa has completed his move to Arsenal

Ezri Konsa has completed his move to Arsenal which means he can team up with Bukayo Saka - who has been vocal in praising his compatriot as one of the best defenders out there.

‌



The Gunners have been in the market for defensive reinforcements and finally secured a deal with Aston Villa for Konsa, who joins for £51million. Arsenal are without the injured William Saliba and Konsa's quality and versatility means he can play across the backline.

‌



Those assets have helped him become a regular in the England picture and it was whilst on international duty that he left his mark on Saka. The duo chose to do extras together, leaving Konsa to try and defend against the Arsenal winger in a one-on-one situation.

‌



Saka was open about his admiration for Konsa, with his comments coming back in 2024, and Konsa was touched to hear praise from such a respected player.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Konsa recalled the incident: “I think it was a couple of years ago with England, we did some one-on-one sessions, me against him, and yeah, I gave him a good test. I take a lot of pride in defending, I love defending so to hear that praise from him is nice.”

‌



The England international will come into a defensive unit that includes the likes of Saliba, Gabriel, Jurrien Timber and Piero Hincapie. They are regarded among the best in Europe and last season kept 19 Premier League clean sheets as Arsenal finally ended their wait for title glory.

Arsenal's defensive quality was also key in them making the Champions League final and Konsa wants to compliment what they have at the Emirates.

View 2 Images Ezri Konsa and Bukayo Saka have been England team-mates for several years

‌



He told the club's website: “The chemistry they have, they all want to defend for each other, the love they have for defending, they love keeping the ball out of the net which is what you have to do as a defender. But I just love the way they are together. What they've built over the past few years has been special.”

Konsa's move means he joins the likes of Bruno Guimaraes and Christos Tzolis in moving to north London this summer. Mikel Arteta is also understood to be eyeing another attacking addition before the transfer window shuts.

Sports.title: Argentina star slapped with 10-MATCH ban as FIFA announce World Cup punishments
Sports.content:
Argentina star slapped with 10-MATCH ban as FIFA announce World Cup punishments

Argentina star Leandro Paredes has been handed a 10-match ban whilst compatriot Nahuel Molina has been banned for seven games following their parts in the brawl that occurred after the World Cup final

View 2 Images Leandro Paredes has been handed a 10 match ban following the unsavoury scenes that followed the World Cup final

FIFA has banned Argentina duo Leandro Paredes and Nahuel Molina for their parts in the brawl that occurred following the World Cup final.

‌



Paredes has been hit with a mammoth 10-match ban whilst Nahuel Molina has been handed a ban of seven matches. One-match bans have been handed down to Thiago Almada and Pablo Martín Páez Gavira.

‌



Paredes and Molina both copped particular criticism for their reactions after Argentina were beaten 1-0 by Spain in the final in New York.

‌



Paredes was caught on camera grabbing Eric Garcia by the throat and throwing Gavi to the ground. Molina was seen striking Rodri as he ran to celebrate.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Former Argentina great Roberto Ayala, who is now part of the staff with his country, was also involved in the post-match scenes and has been hit with a three-match ban whilst Spain midfielder Gavi has had to cop a one-match ban.

‌



FIFA has also fined the Argentina FA $121,000 (£88,700) after their players displayed a Falklands banner following their semi-final win over England and for discrimination and racist abuse by fans.

Argentina won $34m (£24.9m) of prize money during the World Cup but it has been confirmed that $100,000 (£73,000) has to be spent on anti-discrimination campaign whilst another $100,000 (£73,000) of fine was suspended.

View 2 Images Nahuel Molina hit Spain midfielder Rodri as he ran past him to celebrate winning the World Cup

‌



The South Americans had been seeking to defend their World Cup title, which would've made them the first time since Brazil in 1962 to do so, but they were wholly outclassed by Spain.

Enzo Fernandez was sent-off during the game with Ferran Torres scoring the winner for the Euro 2024 champions in extra-time.

In the immediate aftermath Wayne Rooney, part of the BBC coverage, said: "Does it surprise you? It doesn't surprise me. We've seen this with Argentina before. It's just not the reaction you want. We've seen some of the reaction after knocking England out in the last round. That's just sad. If you lose a game of football, be graceful and get out of there. It's really poor from them."

Article continues below

Gary Neville, who was on ITV, echoed that sentiment as he claimed: "They're very competitive and I love that element of them, but [Paredes] has just been a disgrace for the last couple of games, and why the referees have allowed him to continue doing what he is doing..."

Sports.title: Root: England's bowlers don't know how good they can be
Sports.content:
Joe Root was thrilled by the performances of his bowlers as England's pace attack dismissed Pakistan for 135 before tea, to seal a statement three-day victory in the first Test at Headingley.

Pakistan were bowled out for 171 in 48.1 overs on day one, with England responding with an insuperable 409, as they romped their way to victory by an innings and 103 runs, in what was a dream start for Root in his second spell as captain.

On day three, Ollie Robinson (3-29), Jofra Archer (3-50) and Josh Tongue (3-43) seized full advantage of a worn Headingley pitch as they took three wickets apiece, while Gus Atkinson (1-11) followed up with a wicket of his own.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England head to Lord's 1-0 up in the series after beating Pakistan in the first Test by an innings and 103 runs

Root hailed his bowlers after the victory, claiming they "don't know just how good they can be".

"I don't think our bowlers understand well that they complement each other in these conditions, and what they're capable of doing," the Yorkshireman said.

"It's really nice for them to see that and to start the series like that."

Archer, who went wicketless in Pakistan's first innings, got England off to a flying start, dismissing both Pakistan openers, Azan Awais and Imam-ul-Haq inside four overs.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jofra Archer got England off to a flying start on day three, dismissing both Pakistan opening batters Azan Awais and Imam-ul-Haq

Tongue and Robinson were prolific throughout the match, with both completing eight-wicket hauls.

Robinson, the pick of the bowlers, has now won man-of-the-match awards in the two Tests he has played this summer, and Root hailed the 32-year-old for his ability to keep threatening Pakistan's batters late into the match.

"I thought Robinson was brilliant," Root said.

"The fact that he's still as effective in the second innings, having bowled 18 overs, and his understanding of what his requirements are in different phases of the game is important.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The England captain hailed man-of-the-match Ollie Robinson for his exceptional performance

"For him to be effective as the pitch changed throughout and to consistently keep asking difficult questions is a really good sign for us."

'It's always important to win a Test match'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player After a four-year hiatus, Root enjoyed a dream return as England captain, but said things were different

After a chaotic few months, following the departures of former captain Ben Stokes and head coach Brendon McCullum, Root, who was trapped lbw for 66 on day two, stressed the importance of the victory.

But he added England were eager to "not get too carried away".

"It's always important to win a Test match," Root said.

"You're playing for England, right? It's what you set out to do every time you walk out on to that field.

"It's more the fact that we delivered on everything we spoke about, that's the most pleasing thing and the most enjoyable thing about all of it.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Root was dismissed for 66 runs off 112 deliveries on day two

"There's also an understanding that this is one game; there's going to be other challenges and different things to manage. That's the exciting part, and it's taking the confidence from this and being skilful to deal with that next thing, which will be Lord's."

After returning to captain England following a four-year hiatus, Root said things were different this time around.

"It was quite easy on occasion to leave Jimmy Anderson and Stuart Broad to it," Root said, reflecting on his previous spell as captain. "Very experienced, they knew how they were going to operate.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Josh Tongue also impressed with the ball taking eight wickets during the match

"There's a lot of different things this time round.

"I'm very different as well. With everything going on around the Test match it was important to give as much clarity and simplicity to what we were trying to achieve and we delivered on that brilliantly."

Root in contact with Fleming every day

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Stephen Fleming is set to take charge of England after the Pakistan series

Root also revealed incumbent England head coach Stephen Fleming has been in contact with him "every day".

Fleming will not take up the new role until after England's three-match series against Pakistan.

"He's kept tabs on things," Root said.

"It's just been great to have him on the end of the phone and I can speak to him as much or as little as I like.

"It's great that he's very invested already in what we're trying to achieve and there's been constant communication with Marcus Trescothick and me."

Sports.title: Brighton reject £60m Liverpool bid for Minteh
Sports.content:
Brighton have rejected a £60m bid from Liverpool for winger Yankuba Minteh.

Sky Sports News understands the proposal did not meet Brighton's valuation after the Reds previously failed with a £50m bid for the 22-year-old.

Minteh is currently unavailable due to an injury, which is likely to keep him out until October. Brighton are also without Kaoru Mitoma, who has been sidelined since May with a hamstring injury.

Brighton are also in talks with Manchester United over the sale of Carlos Baleba, with an agreement understood to be close over a deal worth in excess of £60m.

Liverpool prioritising reinforcements out wide

Reinforcing in wide-forward areas has been Liverpool's priority throughout this window after already signing Victor Munoz from Osasuna earlier in the window.

As part of Liverpool's process to add in wide areas, they are looking at a number of possibilities, one of those being Minteh.

Liverpool have been pursuing Bradley Barcola at Paris Saint-Germain and remain in contact with the European champions over a deal.

However, PSG's £145m valuation is a complicating factor as Liverpool do not currently want to reach that figure.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Transfer Talk podcast panel discuss Bradley Barcola's potential move to Liverpool and whether or not the French forward would live up to the big money expectations.

Hurzeler: It's normal to have players linked with moves

Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler says it is normal for players to be linked away with moves given the success of the Seagulls across recent season.

Minteh and Baleba are the latest Brighton players to attract transfer interest, after already losing Jan Paul van Hecke to Tottenham and Danny Welbeck to Chelsea earlier in the window.

Speaking ahead of their season opener against Aston Villa on Sunday, live on Sky Sports, Hurzeler said: "We know in general, all the players who there are rumours about are important players, they've been part of the journey over the last two years.

Brighton and Hove Albion

Aston Villa Sunday 23rd August 1:00pm Kick off 2:00pm

"It's normal that if a team is doing well, then there will be a big ask for players. That's part of my job here, it's part of our identity.

"We can go through every individual player, we know how important they are but we know good achievements, big achievements, you create a lot of attention and therefore we have to wait now.

"The situation will evolve. I'm not here to complain, I'm here to find solutions."

Sports.title: Kevin Blake's York tips: Ebor Festival day four picks
Sports.content:
Sky Sports Racing's Kevin Blake reveals a trio of picks as York's Ebor Festival concludes with yet another wildly-competitive card on day four on Saturday.

York have been unlucky with the weather this week, and the softening ground has created some extra challenges, but all being well we can hopefully finish the week on a high.

The Sky Bet Strensall Stakes (1:50) is the first race of interest, and one that looks overpriced is the Hamad Al Jehani-trained Archivist. Long-term readers may recall that I put him up as my selection in the Royal Hunt Cup at Royal Ascot and while it didn't work out for him on the day, he gained compensation on his very next start when overcoming what was considered a near impossible draw of 20 in the Golden Mile at Glorious Goodwood.

Not only did he overcome his draw, he did it with a bit to spare and that performance signalled his readiness to be competitive at stakes level. This course and distance should suit him well and any ease in the ground shouldn't be overly inconvenient for him. He is drawn a little wider than ideal, but that is bearable given his price is so big. A big run from him wouldn't at all surprise.

The Sky Bet Constantine Handicap (4:10) is another extremely tough sprint handicap, but I'm game to have a swing at the Andrew Balding-trained Dance In The Storm. The manner in which the betting markets have been so positive about her in her four starts this season has strongly suggested that she is considered better than a handicapper.

While she has won two of her four starts over seven furlongs this season, she has very much been shaping as though she is worth a try at this shorter trip. She has a career-high mark to overcome, but this different distance could well unlock notable further improvement. She is a really interesting contender and warrants support.

The final selection of the week comes in the concluding Sky Bet Dav Reid Finale Handicap (5:20), and it is the Ger Lyons-trained Diego El Queso. The four-year-old has a progressive profile, winning a handicap at Leopardstown in good style back in April prior to having an absence of 12 weeks that suggests he may have had a hold up.

He returned to action with a tremendous run to finish second to Thread Of Gold in a valuable handicap back at Leopardstown and that form has been well advertised by the winner since then. He was well fancied for a similar race to this at Glorious Goodwood, but the race went wrong for him, yet he still managed to catch the eye in finishing sixth.

He is capable of better than he was able to show there and with both this course and distance and the ease in the ground all promising to suit him, he can be expected to make a bold bid for compensation.

Sports.title: Bacio blazes a trail to win York's Nunthorpe Stakes
Sports.content:
American raider Bacio blitzed his rivals from the front to provide Wesley Ward with a first victory in the Coolmore City Of Troy Nunthorpe Stakes at York.

While the popular Keeneland-based trainer has enjoyed 13 winners at Royal Ascot, success on the Knavesmire has proved elusive, having saddled Acapulco to finish second in 2015 and come even closer two years later through Lady Aurelia, with Frankie Dettori memorably celebrating passing the post only to find he had actually been beaten a nose by Marsha.

Bacio was the 3/1 favourite to go one better under Juan Hernandez following a brilliant victory in the Palace of Holyroodhouse at the Royal meeting in June and pre-race concerns about the rain-softened ground soon proved unfounded as the three-year-old flew out of the starting stalls.

He had most of his rivals struggling to keep up from halfway and never really looked in any danger of being reeled in, passing the post a length and a quarter clear of Starlust.

No sooner had Hernandez piloted an aeroplane up the York straight he had to run back to the weighing room as he needed to make a sharp exit, with a 6.30pm flight back to America from Heathrow to Los Angeles ahead of the Pacific Classic at Del Mar.

To make sure he made that flight, Hernandez first had to take a helicopter ride from the middle of the Knavesmire to Heathrow and he did not have a minute to spare.

While running back for a brief presentation of the trophies from the Queen, he said: "The horse was giving everything and he'd trained really good.

"He shipped really well, I know a lot of people were worried about the ground for him but he didn't know that.

"He ran great, he broke out of the gate really well, really sharp and he was ready to go. When the gate opened, he was all fire. He was trying to go too early, but I was able to take him back a little bit and save him for the last part.

"He won the race from the gate. Everyone here has done such a great job with the horse. I'm really happy, this race is for America and all my family. Thank you guys!"

Arapaho Gold stays unbeaten in Gimcrack

Arapaho Gold stretched his unbeaten record to four with victory in the Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Gimcrack Stakes.

The Michael Dods-trained gelding won a couple of low-key races at Thirsk either side of being withdrawn after playing up in the stalls at Beverley, since when he had successfully graduated to Listed company in the Rose Bowl at Newbury.

He faced another step up in class for this prestigious Group Two contest, but proved more than up to the task in the hands of Connor Beasley, briefly coming under pressure before getting himself organised and finishing strongly to repel Final Objective by three-quarters of a length at 2/1.

Image: Arapaho Gold, ridden by Connor Beasley, on their way to winning the Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Gimcrack at York

Darlington-based Dods has enjoyed some of the best days of his career at York, having saddled Mecca's Angel to win her second Nunthorpe on this day 10 years ago, while he also sent out the popular sprinter Dakota Gold to win on the Knavesmire six times.

"Once he was out and running I was happy. At halfway he was looking for a bit of room, but once the room came he really quickened up," said Dods.

"Connor just said the last 100 yards he gave him some feel the way he quickened away from them. He's a good horse, this was a big step up and he's taken everything in his stride. When we've wanted him to step up he has and he has stepped up again there. He's just some horse isn't he?"

On future plans, Dods added: "He'll go to the Mill Reef (at Newbury) now and that will probably be it for the season and we'll see where we go next year.

"He's got the speed for six furlongs as you've just seen and I don't think you'll see any problems getting seven. He quickens up and he gallops. It's an interesting problem (planning), but we'll deal with it. He's an exciting horse to have and it's brilliant that we've got him in the yard.

"We've had a lot of luck at York, but this is right up there with the two Mecca's Angel wins and winning that is unbelievable."

Richard Brown, racing advisor to Wathnan Racing, who own the runner-up Final Objective, said: "It was a massive run, it's one where you are delighted because the horse has run a huge race.

"A furlong out I thought he was coming to win, he hasn't been straightforward and Hamad (Al Jehani) has done a great job training this horse and that is a career best, so we'll keep him busy.

"He wandered about when he won at Thirsk last week and he has done again, so I think we'll pop a pair of cheekpieces on.

"There's a race in France, the Prix Eclipse, that we could look at, but we'll all have a sit down and see what might be best for him."

Adrian Keatley said of the third home, Hell Of A Spin: "He's a hardy little horse who tries his heart out and he's running consistently well in these good races.

"You'd like to think there's a nice one in him one of these days, I don't think the trip or ground were a concern for him, it was just the winner quickened away.

"He's been placed in a Molecomb and Gimcrack now. There could be a race in France towards the back-end for him - we'll keep trying."

Sports.title: Russell claims Dutch GP Sprint pole with Antonelli, Hamilton on back foot
Sports.content:
George Russell made the ideal start to his attempt to mount a championship fightback in the second half of the 2026 F1 season by claiming pole position for Saturday's Dutch Grand Prix Sprint as nearest title rivals Kimi Antonelli and Lewis Hamilton qualified outside the top four.

On F1's first day back on track after the sport's four-week summer break, Russell claimed his third Sprint pole in five attempts this season as his final SQ3 lap of 1:11.567 beat McLaren's Lando Norris and Ferrari's Charles Leclerc to the head of the weekend's first Zandvoort grid by under a tenth of a second.

But championship leader Antonelli was only fifth quickest in the other Mercedes, the Italian teenager's session compromised after he damaged his car in a trip through the gravel on his first lap of SQ1.

Hamilton, who is second to Antonelli in the standings, qualified only seventh in the second Ferrari after earlier promise on Friday faded.

Hamilton trails Antonelli by 50 points in the Drivers' Championship, with Russell a further nine points adrift. Points are on offer to the top-eight finishers in Saturday's 24-lap Sprint, which starts at 11am on Sky Sports F1, with eight for the winner.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli suffered a nervy moment as he went off into the gravel during SQ1

Russell got engaged to his long-time partner Carmen Montero Mundt during F1's break and quipped on Mercedes team radio after his Sprint pole was confirmed: "Nice one! Must be a bit lighter after that engagement ring!"

Oscar Piastri took fourth in the second McLaren, just 0.009s back on pole himself, with Max Verstappen sixth for Red Bull at his home event - but half a second away from the front amid a disappointing opening day for Red Bull.

Indeed, Verstappen and seventh-placed Hamilton lapped closer to Alpine's Pierre Gasly - whose car has the Enstone team's sole upgrade this weekend - than the polesitter.

Eighth-placed Gasly led the midfield fight ahead of Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto in ninth and Racing Bulls' Arvid Linbdlad in 10th.

2) Lando Norris, McLaren

5) Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes



6) Max Verstappen, Red Bull

10) Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls

Lindblad denied Liam Lawson, his usual Racing Bulls' team-mate but who is racing for the senior Red Bull team this weekend in place of the injured Isack Hadjar, the last top-10 berth on the final laps of SQ2

Lawson, who had two ill-fated races for Red Bull at the start of last season, outpaced Verstappen in the first session but lost out on a SQ3 berth by three tenths of a second.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell pipped Lando Norris for Sprint pole at the Dutch Grand Prix

The New Zealander will start just ahead of Yuki Tsunoda, the driver who is standing in for him this weekend at Racing Bulls, with the Japanese qualifying 12th on his first F1 race weekend since December.

Fernando Alonso qualified last in the Aston Martin - which features Honda's long-awaited first engine upgrade as well as a second round of aerodynamic revisions - after a problem with his AMR26's straight-line mode cost him crucial lap time. The Spanish veteran had finished 12th fastest in the only practice session.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A downhearted Lewis Hamilton says that Sprint Qualifying at the Dutch Grand Prix was 'not a good session' for him.

Russell 'really happy to come back' as Antonelli mistake proves costly

Russell's pole position lap at the end of SQ3 came as something of a surprise given the Briton had only lapped fifth and fourth-fastest respectively in the first two knockout segments, two tenths off the pace, with Ferrari and McLaren appearing to have the legs on championship leaders Mercedes.

But Russell proved a more competitive proposition on the mandatory, and single, soft-tyre runs of the final phase to deny McLaren rival Norris the fastest time.

"It was a tough end to the first half of the year and I'm really happy to come back," said Russell, who scored only six points in the two races before the summer break.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell admitted it was a good reminder to himself that he's 'still got it' having taken Sprint pole at the Dutch Grand Prix.

"The lap felt really good. It all came together really nicely. It's always difficult these Sprint Qualifyings with just one shot on the soft tyre. The track always takes a step, the grip takes a step.

"McLaren look quick, Ferrari look quick but I'm glad to pull it off when it matted."

Unusually Antonelli did not finish in the top four of any of the three qualifying segments, confirming afterwards that his slide wide through the gravel at the penultimate corner on his first timed lap of SQ1 had damaged the underside of his W17.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris says he is 'reasonably happy' with P2 in Sprint Qualifying at the Dutch Grand Prix, but admits he plans to fight George Russell for the win.

"Oh yeah, [there was] big time [damage]. I had a couple of holes in the floor," Antonelli said.

"When I came in, they initially said it was a loss of 25 [downforce] points. They tried to repair as much as possible, but definitely the damage was still there. I was struggling a lot in the low-speed [corners].

"It is what it is. It was a little bit too much entry speed in the last corner on that first lap. I lost the rear and went through the gravel, and that was pretty much it.

"And then obviously it was not easy to build the confidence back. But still decently close, and we'll have another go tomorrow."

Sports.title: Draper ruled out of US Open as injury absence continues
Sports.content:
British star Jack Draper has been ruled out of the US Open as he continues to battle a bone bruise in his dominant left arm.

After two dispiriting matches in the United States, Draper has concluded he needs more time to recover, according to sources close to the player.

The news, which came only a couple of hours after world No 1 Jannik Sinner announced he would miss the tournament with a knee injury, while Carlos Alcaraz is set to make his return after a four-month spell on the sidelines with a wrist injury.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Cincinnati Open match between Draper and Martin Landaluce

The former world No 4, who has not played at a single Grand Slam this year, said he was in a "difficult place" after his first-round defeat by Martin Landaluce in the Cincinnati Open last week, admitting he was struggling to escape the mental fatigue that had built up during 15 months of battling serious injury.

Draper told the Guardian: "It's the same as last week, the way I'm usually able to fight for every ball and conduct myself, it's just missing.

"Obviously, the conditions and all the things that I'm changing is very hard to manage, but I think from just an internal point of view, it's a difficult place to be right now."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Annabel Croft and Ryan Harrison say they feel for Draper as he battles ongoing injury setbacks

Draper has made a series of changes to reduce the strain on his left arm. Since Wimbledon, the 24-year-old has altered his strings and racket, while continuing to tweak his service motion.

He admitted managing it is a constant challenge, saying: "It's got to a point with me where it's taken probably one of my biggest qualities, my fighting spirit.

"There's a level of chronic pain that's always with you. When you've got that on your playing arm - this is my life, this is my career, you know?

"When you've got an injury that is tough to come past and tough to understand, there's many challenges, there's many obstacles."

Croft: Draper needs to try and fix his body!

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Draper was in tears on his return from injury at the Canadian Open

Speaking to Gigi Salmon on Sky Sports Tennis, Annabel Croft said it was a bit of "doom and gloom" around tennis at the moment.

"Maybe we weren't so surprised," said the former British No 1. "We knew something was up when we saw that eruption of emotion just a couple of events ago. I got the impression this horrible long-term injury - the bone bruising in his arm just wasn't going away - it was rearing its ugly head again and he spoke quite openly about it.

"He's tried everything and it just keeps coming back, so maybe this is a good decision because to go into a Grand Slam, it's best of five sets and it's absolutely brutal.

"It's seven matches back-to-back and they've looked at that and decided he's not ready for that.

"He needs to go away and try - I don't know how - to fix his body. It's been so emotional for him because he wants to go out there and compete.

"The US Open is a Grand Slam where he has reached the semi-finals. He has challenged all of the very best in the world, so I feel very sad for him."

Draper's injury timeline after Wimbledon 2025...

July-Aug 2025 : Break until the US Open

: Break until the US Open Aug 2025: US Open mixed doubles, then one singles match before withdrawing with a left-arm injury

US Open mixed doubles, then one singles match before withdrawing with a left-arm injury Sep 2025-Jan 2026: Out injured

Out injured Feb 2026: Returned to competition

Returned to competition Apr 2026: Retired in Barcelona with a knee injury and was out for more than two months.

Retired in Barcelona with a knee injury and was out for more than two months. June 2026: Returned at Eastbourne; then withdrew from Wimbledon

Returned at Eastbourne; then withdrew from Wimbledon Aug 2026: Returned at Montreal and Cincinnati

Returned at Montreal and Cincinnati Aug 21, 2026: Withdrew from the US Open with his left-arm injury

What's happening to tennis? Has it become too long and relentless?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Draper opens up about the mental and physical challenges of his recent injury

Former player turned coach, Ryan Harrison said: "It's 11 months and it's non-stop. The year-end championship comes along in November, which is such a big event with the prestige to try and finish world No 1. We saw a world No 1 race right to the very end last year between Sinner and Alcaraz. There's a lot of incentive there to try and get to that top spot but for me it's the way the courts are playing and the way the balls are playing now.

"It's not as friendly to big serving and it's not as friendly to points being quick anymore because the courts have slowed down, while the conditions have slowed down so we're seeing a lot more longer, physical rallies, and that's more physically demanding on the body.

"I think it's even more difficult to stay healthy now than it was say 20 or 30 years ago when the courts were more friendly to service winners and aces.

"Nowadays, the 11 months, the physicality, the demands of the tour. We love seeing these epic matches and epic rallies, but the body pays for that price."

Does change need to happen?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Draper reflected on his battles with injury after returning to action and speaks of the influence that Andy Murray has had on a difficult period in his career

Croft said: "It's very difficult to change the calendar because so many of the tournaments are individually owned and you have all the sponsorship around that. It's difficult to take it away!

"It does feel the surfaces have all been coming together a lot more and there wasn't so much definition. I think a lot of the players would like to see a lot of the courts quickened up."

Sports.title: Russell: Sprint pole a good reminder that 'I've still got it'
Sports.content:
George Russell admitted it was "good to remind myself I've still got it" after returning to form by taking Sprint pole for the Dutch Grand Prix.

Having begun the season as the clear favourite for the drivers' title, Russell has endured a tumultuous campaign which has seen him unexpectedly outperformed by his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli.

Antonelli arrived in Zandvoort, the first event after the sport's summer break, with a 50-point lead over Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton at the top of the Drivers' Championship, with Russell a further nine points adrift in third.

Knowing he needs a major turnaround to fight back in the title race, Russell made the perfect start on Friday by beating McLaren's Lando Norris to Sprint pole after Antonelli took himself out of contention by damaging his car in the gravel in the first part of the session.

Russell said: "It's been a little while since I've been top of the timesheets in any session. I can't even remember the last time.

"It's good to remind myself I've still got it and haven't forgotten how to drive. The break came at a good point."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell admitted it was a good reminder to himself that he has 'still got it' having taken Sprint pole at the Dutch Grand Prix

Russell edged out Norris by four hundredths of a second, with Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and the other McLaren of Oscar Piastri also finishing within a tenth of the Brit's leading time.

"Of course it's only the Sprint," Russell added. "Qualifying will be the key one and McLaren look really fast and Ferrari look quick.

"It's been a real surprise to us as a team these past couple of races. We are in a good spot."

Russell appeared to run out of ideas as the summer break approached, with the 28-year-old publicly flip-flopping on whether his driving style was the reason he was struggling to match Antonelli, who is competing in just his second F1 season and only turns 20 two days after Sunday's race.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Russell pipped Lando Norris for Sprint pole

"I came into this weekend with a real open mind because I had no idea how it would go. My confidence level wasn't exactly at my highest," Russell said.

"I just tried to remember that feeling of what I needed from myself and the car - almost treating it like the first race of the season again and not overthink things. That seems to have worked well for me.

"It's very difficult to actually put those words into action but I know when I'm in the right frame of mind, come Q3 I can always deliver, it's just ensuring I'm in the right frame of mind ahead of that point."

Antonelli says 'big-time' damage cost him

Antonelli had topped the weekend's sole practice to establish himself as favourite for Sprint pole but made an unnecessary error in the first part of qualifying.

Pushing hard on his first lap in SQ1, Antonelli lost control of his car at the final corner and actually did well to stay pointing forward and avoid becoming beached in the gravel.

Antonelli was able to comfortably advance through SQ1 and SQ2 despite Mercedes finding holes in the floor of his car, but was two tenths off Russell in SQ3 as he finished fifth.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli suffered a nervy moment as he went off into the gravel during SQ1

Asked if the damage had impacted him, Antonelli told Sky Sports F1: "Oh yeah, big time. I had a couple of holes in the floor.

"When I came in, they initially said it was a loss of 25 [downforce] points. They tried to repair as much as possible, but definitely the damage was still there. I was struggling a lot in the low-speed [corners].

"It is what it is. It was a little bit too much entry speed in the last corner on that first lap. I lost the rear and went through the gravel, and that was pretty much it.

"And then obviously it was not easy to build the confidence back. But still decently close, and we'll have another go tomorrow."

Wolff: Pressure off Russell's shoulders after engagement!

Mercedes chief Toto Wolff suggested Russell may have benefitted from getting engaged to his long-term partner Carmen Montero Mundt during the summer break.

Wolff told Sky Sports F1: "George is coming back. I think he feels so much pressure is off his shoulders after she accepted his marriage proposal!

"Some solid work on the day to day, he put the dots together and had a very good lap."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Russell discusses his engagement to partner Carmen and aims a funny jibe Lando Norris' way!

Wolff appeared to play down the extent of the damage to Antonelli's car, suggesting Mercedes had largely repaired the issue ahead of SQ3.

"Kimi lost 20 points [of downforce] with a hole in the floor but we managed to patch it up and it looked like it was completely intact afterwards," Wolff said.

"The gaps are so close and he made a little bit of a mistake at Turn 11, pushing too hard on the entry, and it can go quickly."
